topic: Venus's rotation is so slow its day outlasts its year
title: A Year on Venus Ends Before a Single Day Does
description: Venus takes longer to spin once than it does to orbit the Sun -- a real astronomical oddity explained in under a minute. AI-narrated commentary, part of an ongoing series covering strange, verifiable facts about space, science, history, and psychology.

hook_candidates.text: Venus finishes an entire year before it finishes spinning once.
What happens to a planet that spins so slowly its own year finishes first?
You'd assume every planet spins faster than it orbits. Venus doesn't.
When scientists first clocked Venus's rotation, they found something that shouldn't be possible: a planet that can't finish one spin before its year is already over.

payoff_mechanism: Venus's atmosphere is roughly 90 times thicker than Earth's, and constant solar heating creates a thermal tide inside that thick air which pulls backward against the planet's rotation hard enough to nearly cancel out its spin entirely.

beats.text: Venus finishes an entire **year** before it finishes spinning once.
One day on Venus lasts **243** Earth days. Its whole year only takes 225.

That's because Venus's air is almost **100** times thicker than Earth's, and the Sun heats it hard enough to create a tide inside the atmosphere itself that drags backward against the planet's spin, nearly canceling it out.
So Venus never even finishes one **spin** before its next lap around the Sun starts. Follow for more space rules that quietly break basic math.
